chunks: The eminent Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us from Yusuf b. al-Harith from Muhammad b. Mihran from Ali b. al-Hasan. He said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us from Ma'mar from Isma'il b. Mu'awiya from Nafi' from Ibn Umar. He said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: On the Day of Resurrection, the Throne of the Lord of the Worlds will be adorned with every adornment. Then two pulpits of light — each a hundred miles in height — will be brought forth. One will be placed to the right of the Throne and the other to the left of the Throne. Then al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them) will be brought forth. Al-Hasan will stand upon one of them and al-Husayn upon the other. The Lord, blessed and exalted, adorns His Throne with them just as a woman adorns herself with her earrings.

key_terms.عرش: Throne — the Throne of God, the supreme station in Islamic cosmology
key_terms.قرطاها: her earrings — dual form, used as a simile for the two grandsons adorning the Throne
key_terms.منبر: pulpit — an elevated platform, here described as being made of light
key_terms.نور: light — divine luminescence, frequently associated with the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.يوم القيامة: Day of Resurrection — the eschatological day of final judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the status of Hasan and Husayn on the Day of Resurrection according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, the Prophet Muhammad (S) describes the exalted status of his grandsons al-Hasan and al-Husayn on the Day of Resurrection. Two luminous pulpits of immense height will be placed flanking the Throne of God, and the two Imams will stand upon them. The Prophet uses a vivid simile: God adorns His Throne with Hasan and Husayn just as a woman adorns herself with her earrings, conveying their supreme closeness to the divine and their role as ornaments of the celestial realm.
